headline: On last trading day, Sensex dropped 1,484 points amid heavy selling in banking and metal stocks.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Wednesday, 25 November.

why: Indian stock markets are closed on Tuesday, November 24, on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti.
In the previous session, Sensex fell 1,484 points due to heavy selling pressure in banking and metal stocks.
Global market cues remained weak during the last trading session.
FII buying continued for 16 consecutive sessions, with net inflows of ₹5,672.99 crore despite market decline.
whatHappening: Adani Group is planning a capital expenditure of $120 billion over the next 5-6 years, as per Jefferies.
Vedanta is seeking a premium over imported LNG prices for its Rajasthan gas sales.
The government plans to sell part of its stake in IIFCL via an IPO alongside fresh share issuance.
RBI Deputy Governor urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in G-Sec underwriting auctions.
summary:
Indian share markets are closed on Tuesday, November 24, for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
In the last trading session, the Sensex dropped 1,484 points led by losses in metal and banking stocks.
Corporate developments included Adani Group's $120 billion capex plan and Vedanta's gas pricing moves.
